findings: The dated guide lists 60 EC in each year. Four introductory language modules total 24 EC, two subsequent language-and-literature modules add 12 EC, and the 30 EC exchange includes at least 12 EC of language study. The abroad entry lists Athens first, then Thessaloniki, with 18 further EC in relevant regional subjects. The generic public mention of Cyprus is not used to instantiate this route.

The first language-and-literature entry requires A2, supplied by year-one progression. Greece, Cyprus and Europe requires Greek and Dutch at B1 and uses Greek journalistic texts. The first two years, including B1-or-higher language work in Athens, prepare for it. The thesis requires completion of both years one and two and is a 12 EC individual study with oral presentation. The thirty elective EC, thesis and eighteen thematic EC are distinct. Tutoring and the writing diagnostic are uncredited. Ordinary full-time BSA is 48 first-year EC under the faculty regulation.

The literary trial gives weight to Greek myth and tragedy, ancient heritage, stylistics, general language-processing methods and cultural interpretation. The historical trial adds imperial and modern history, social theory, memory and source methods; the political trial adds EU law and institutions, conflict and public policy. These are real academic contributions. None supplies the regional depth across modern Greece and Cyprus, Greek-language sources and literary-cultural inquiry that defines this programme. Feasibility succeeded for each complete trial, so the no-match is an academic decision.
